title: TrendComparisonOutput
description: Structured output from the trend-comparator skill summarising how a problem has changed across time or regions.

topic.description: The problem category being compared (e.g., 'water supply failures', 'air quality', 'flooding').

comparison_type.description: Whether the comparison is across time (temporal), across regions (spatial), or both.

arm_1.description: Description of the baseline comparison arm.

label.description: Human-readable label for this arm (e.g., 'City A, 2024' or 'Region X').

affected_people.description: Estimated affected population in this arm.

article_count.description: Number of news articles used for this arm.

people_change_pct.description: Percentage change in affected population from arm_1 to arm_2. Null if arm_1.affected_people is 0.

severity_delta.description: Change in severity rank (low=1, medium=2, high=3, critical=4). Positive means escalation.

trend.description: Overall trend classification derived from people_change_pct and severity_delta.

confidence.description: Confidence in the trend classification: 0.0 (inconclusive) to 1.0 (high confidence). See trend_signals.md for thresholds.

key_differences.description: Bullet-point factual differences between the two arms. Each item is a single, specific observation.
examples: Severity escalated from medium to high
New sub-problem emerged: contamination of backup reservoir

insights.description: Interpretive statements explaining what the differences mean and why. Each item is a sentence or short paragraph.
examples: The 40% increase in affected population suggests the infrastructure problem is structural, not event-driven.
The severity escalation to 'high' means the issue now qualifies for emergency budget allocation.
Article volume increased proportionally, reducing the risk of a coverage-inflation artifact.

anomalies.description: List of detected anomaly signals (see trend_signals.md) that may affect reliability of the trend classification.
examples: Arm 2 article count is 3× higher than Arm 1 — possible media attention surge
Comparison spans different seasons — seasonal variation may inflate change

recommendation.description: Single recommended action based on the trend, surfaced in the UI.
examples: Escalate to a high-priority solution generation task; the rising trend suggests deterioration will continue without intervention.

key_differences: Severity escalated from medium to high
New sub-problem detected in 2025: contamination of backup reservoir during flood events
insights: The consistent 40% increase in affected residents across two non-catastrophic years indicates a structural deterioration in stormwater infrastructure, not an event-driven spike.
Severity escalation to 'high' means the problem now meets the threshold for emergency budget allocation.
The emergence of reservoir contamination as a secondary problem suggests cascading infrastructure failure if no intervention occurs.
examples.recommendation: Escalate to high-priority solution generation. Rising trend with severity escalation; deterioration will continue without infrastructure investment.
